commentBody: Congratulations on creating a puzzle that was clever and fun to solve!

Some bonus theme-adjacent answers in the puzzle!

“Comes with air compressor in the trunk for just in case”  
FREELOAD

“Cost for long distance trips that you can only safely do on back roads” 
TOLL FREE

“Requirement for a visit to every town’s mechanic” 
SIDE TRIP

“How you’ll feel once you get this beauty home” 
- ISSED
( which I filled in 41A incorrectly, heh heh)
Humblebragging 37 minutes FASTER than my average. Frankly, I'm not THAT bright.
Very clever! But I finished it in just a few minutes so what do I do with the rest of my Saturday night? ;)

I love it when with these stats it's called Average!

What a hoot!  Very funny theme clues/answers, many non-theme clues playing on words, a mostly no-stress difficulty level so as not to blunt the fun, and lovely answers on top of it all – SCAMP, FEIGN, QUASH, WANTON, FOIST, GALLANT, FREELOAD, ANOINT, CODGER.

That’s entertainment!  Way to lift the day, Ralph and Doug -- and with a piece-of-junk car!  Bravo, and thank you both!

Really fun, clever-but-not-too-cute puzzle.

Recently someone mentioned solver satisfaction vs. constructor vanity.  I thought this one was long on solver satisfaction and short on constructor vanity. IMO it should always be that way.
I enjoyed this one a lot. Didn’t need much help. Mostly with names, as always. I hope y’all have a wonderful Sunday!

Who knew wheeling and dealing could be so much fun?  To the constructors I say thanks for the ride.

Fine print at the bottom of the ad …

"We stand behind every car we sell. We’ll help push it."
Thanks for a fun puzzle. Shaved four seconds off my Sunday average.

Congrats on your double debut Ralph and of course you too Doug. Extremely witty and fun puzzle both in the theme and the solve. 

Short notes today since I’m at the Cincinnati soccer game where some folks will also be using their heads (if the storm goes away).

Appreciated some of the other related content like ASIS, “barely runs” and “runs out”.

The Feynman quote was worth the price of admission!

Just asking any Indian commentators here if SARI is pronounced like SORRY, because I don’t.
So, “Sorry, not sari!”
Or, as the Indian gentleman asked his wife who kept buying clothes at a second hand store: “Whose sari now?”

Fun Sunday puzzle. My fastest Sunday solve ever. Probably on the easier side but I felt on the right wavelength with the fun theme!

Loved this puzzle!

Rating:
9/10
Oh, that was hecka fun. A good ride, you might say.
Really funny.  Please construct another for us soon, fellas!

I enjoyed that one, thanks guys. 

But as a Canadian, I couldn't for the life of me think of a SARI homonym that's the name of a board game. 

So after finishing, I checked online and was surprised to find that you Yanks apparently pronounce the "o" in Sorry the same as the "a" in SARI. I'm sahree (😩), but that just sounds so wrong to my ears.

But then, you guys do lots of weird stuff ... at least it doesn't have an 'ou' or 'z' (pronounced 'zed', BTW) in it to be messed with! 😄

[Also BTW, and quoting Google's AI Overview:                  
Canadians typically pronounce "sorry" to rhyme with "sore" (SOAR-ee), rather than sounding like the fabric "sari" (SAH-ree)".]
I'll rate this one as "tow"-rifficly fun. Thanks Ralph and Doug! Here's some music that would probably be appropriate for moving that car: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R9eQkTJZlNk

Witchiepoo (Billie Hayes) may take exception to 45D: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WHJD9hidH7M Ralph and Doug, you have just described most of the rides cruising down Jefferson or Gratiot on a Saturday night.

The themers were so funny and so perfectly related to the clues that they made the puzzle a joy to solve.  Almost no unmasked fills—yes, our beloved cookie was there, but who would dis such a clever clue?

Your puzzle perked up a punishingly hot afternoon, Ralph and Doug. Thank you!

How about the “as-is” crossword?

[“… but what about the fact that the grid is rife with obscure never-heard-of answers?]
[“… or that a number of the answers are misspelled?”]
[“… and many of the hints are so impenetrable it makes me want to scream!”]



FRESH FILL
NOVEL WORDPLAY
ENGAGING CLUES
Sometimes the puzzle leaves me cold but I found these jokes quite funny.

Aha!  Euphemisms!!!!  That's what "SPIN" in the title means!  Cute wordplay on the double meaning of SPIN -- and I should have seen it sooner.

Question: Why was this the most enjoyable puzzle I've ever done -- or probably ever will do -- based on a car theme?  Answer:  Because I didn't need to know one single thing about cars to solve it.  That's my kind of car puzzle!

Poor car.  Such awful things happening to it.  But there weren't any passengers mentioned, so the accident didn't seem too grisly.   I was a little perplexed by the leaky roof leading to BUCKET SEATS.  But then I thought:  they must be real buckets to catch the water.  Yes?

I think that everyone will need crosses to get the theme answers.  Nothing is obvious or telegraphed.  The surrounding fill was hard enough to hold my attention and make me work.  Best of all, the mood of the puzzle is lighthearted and playful and there are almost no names or pop culture.  A fun Sunday.
Wonderful puzzle! Loved it!

Very fun and very fast!! Surprised that I got most of the themers with very few, if any, crosses. They all made me chuckle though. Especially enjoyed BUCKETSEATS.

I would tell you the extraordinarily embarrassing story about the time my husband and I had to use KELESSENTRY for the first time but we have sworn each other to absolute secrecy for the sake of our family name. 

We do have a small MoTE, error MITE of pride, after all. Har!!

Not a huge fan of the punny grids. But this one told a story, so it was much more engaging to me than normal. Also, creative phrases used to sell things is generally interesting, but of course, disingenuous. 

The quote in 35A was amazing. 

Thank you constructors. 


One clue/entry I don’t get it is. 
“Race prior to a race”. REV. 
I’m sure it’s obvious.
That was great. I really enjoyed this puzzle. New shocks and low emissions. Amazing that you can come up with those ideas. Kudus to Ralph Sharaga and Doug Peterson.

44D [What many are bound to say about this puzzle] LOVE IT!! I know I do. The themers didn’t just make me laugh; they were, in my view, ingenious. The Lemon Law might apply to this jalopy, but certainly not the puzzle. Thank you, Ralph and Doug, for the delightful hour I've just spent solving it! For some background music, here are The Cars with "Drive" - https://youtu.be/xuZA6qiJVfU?is=CaJPPzDsMDM0nue4 (in which they ask "Who's gonna drive you home tonight?" and, because I just bought the sorry jam jar, I answer: "AAA?")
Nice one
Fun and easy. Nice after yesterday’s slog.

I really enjoyed this puzzle- yes because it was easier than most but it had me laughing and put me in a good mood. It proves that it does not have to be superhard and yet be extremely clever! Congrats
Just one of the cleanest, most consistent, and satisfying puzzles, very nice.
Hilarious. Fast and fun

I'll be the curmudgeon today. The theme was spectacular, ingenious, and funny. But I found the rest of the puzzle boring and had trouble motivating myself to finish it. Too many 3- and 4-letter words.

Loved this one! It reminded me of the car dealer commercials that aired when I was a kid… No you won’t get a lemon, from Toyota of ORANGE 🤣 https://youtu.be/5KDmB7zB9lU?is=BIeaWOX_aypwtD_u Thank you, Ralph and Doug and congratulations to Ralph on the double debut!! Picked up my daughter from her camp in Wisconsin today - what a couple of weeks she had! Her group headed to Minnesota to hike a portion of the Superior Hiking Trail between Beaver Bay and Silver Bay. Two trees fell on their campsite during the windstorms/tornados. They had to evacuate and take shelter at the Tettegouche State Park visitor center, then finally checked into a hotel for the evening 😱 Glad everyone was safe and really glad she’s with me now 😅
Fast and fun

Cute & funny punny theme!
Sometimes I appreciate a quick Sunday, and even more so when it has something fun!  Thanks, constructors!
Hilarious! 😆 The BUCKET SEATS did me in!

I enjoyed this. The difficulty for me was that of an early morning Wednesday, which I find optimal for a huge Sunday grid. The fill didn't natick me. There was some welcome misdirection in the clues. And I actually quite liked the theme, despite its groany undertones. Nice.

Fun puzzle and made me laugh. 

A few clues though were off. Être means to be not to be with or did you mean in Québec. Concurring with other comments sorry is pronounced sore-ee. Wrong to clue based on specific accent.

A prefect is common in UK schools and any system based on British system (not a clue but wordplay comment).

Not a smooth or easy ride, but an enjoyable one! I had some trouble but no complaints from me, nice playful theme, well executed, lots of good fill. 

One note from across the pond: i think Americans think of all sporty types as ATHLETES, so “Team players” makes sense. But for me (a Brit), the word  is strongly associated with individual stars of track and field like Usain Bolt or Carl Lewis. 

So a slight misdirect, but heyho, I shall suck on a smore as i drink my tea and be thankful for the NYT.
Very fun. Low emissions, Quiet Ride... Nice one!

Fun puzzle, the theme answers were not easily guessed and also funny. At least that was my experience. Couple of sticky areas, a delightful solve in all. The Feynman clue was perfect. I also laughed at IRONED for smooth, now. Caitlin's link on bucket seats sent me down a small rabbit hole on missed features in old cars: https://www.jalopnik.com/these-are-your-favorite-dead-car-trends-1850954943/ One feature I never understood was big wheels plus skinny tires (low profile?). The comment in the article was "I'm tired of cracking wheels on potholes." Really? So people pay a lot extra for a bumpy ride and also fragile wheels? I've hit lots of potholes in my life and have never once damaged a wheel. Obviously I didn't own skinny tires. Now I don't even own a car, but I digress.

Not that easy but good fun. 
'Black rectangle' gave me a shiver though - it reminded me that the judge in a murder trial would put a square of black cloth on his head before he pronounced the death penalty. It's in lots of old British films. 
Prefects, as noted already, are very common in British secondary schools; it's supposed to be an 'honour' for the oldest pupils to help police the younger pupils, and there can be a Head Girl and Head Boy. 

"As flies to wanton boys are we to the gods; they kill us for their sport." is from King Lear.

Very enjoyable! The themers were funny and not at all obvious to me. Each one made it's debut today, so extra points for that. The only song I know about REVERE, from the uber talented Faith Soloway: https://youtu.be/QQTkXhsZtic?si=IgpMzy8CtdRJoShc
I usually strongly dislike this type of puzzle, and Sundays lately have been a slog, so this was a surprising return to easy breezy fun Sundays. All the dad jokes hit for me. Thanks!
I absolutely loved this crossword today!! It really took me for a "spin".
We really enjoyed this puzzle and its delightful cluing! Ralph's comedy background was put to great use. We smiled and chuckled throughout!
This was so funny! Also the first (and probably last) time I've completed a Sunday crossword without having to look anything up. Thank you, a great start to my day. 😀
One of my favorite car songs by the late, great Bill Morrissey: https://youtu.be/YevrGtidvpM?si=djG6LcFB2GKseiNx
Absolutely enjoyed the theme today.
What a fantastic puzzle and a perfect start to a Sunday morning.
Enjoyed everything about this Sunday puzzle! No obvious theme answers. Each one required multiple crosses to figure out , but each was on the mark, very clever and made me smile.😊

The punny car clues were tremendously fun to solve.  Once I got the first one, I did something I don’t usually do: I tried solving them without relying on crosses. What a cheery start to a Sunday morning.
This was incredibly fun! I really loved the theme, very enjoyable puzzle to solve.
What great fun!
Super fun! Really enjoyed this one!
Just wonderful! What a hilarious and fun puzzle.

Easily one of my favorite puzzles of the year. After my first pass, I thought there was no way I was solving without looking up clues. But pass by pass, I built more answers, corrected a few, and ended on the "point of intersection" and "old yeller" for a "clueless" win! 

More from this dynamic constructor duo, please!

Color me surprised.

I was expecting to see a lot of complaints for how easy it was today, but a fun theme goes a long way.

I agree with that assessment. Much closer to my best than my average, but definitely one where the theme added to the fill and the enjoyment.

Congratulations on the debut! Perseverance pays.
Great puzzle. Perfect Sunday fare. Laughed to myself a lot!

That was fun!  The theme clues has me smiling throughout, and my brain got a little workout before breakfast.  Sharks not for me to love here?

Y’all have a happy day and remember to be kind.
Also focused on the themers, which came pretty easily, with the exception of NEWSHOCKS.  Needed more amperage (crosses) for that one.  Well done and congrats on the debut.

This was a lot of fun. Thanks, Ralph and Doug.

Considering the theme, 15D should have skipped the Harry Potter angle and been clued as, simply, Ford.

(Ford PREFECT from the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.)

I'm definitely not a car person, but found this delightful and fun. I liked that the theme answers had to be worked out individually. Nothing really jumped out until the crosses made the answers obvious.

Maybe a little easy for a Sunday, but the size made that perfectly okay. I really enjoyed this one. Congrats to Ralph on his debut. I'll be working the L.A. Times puzzle, too.

Enjoyed the corny theme today, but, alas, the puzzle almost solved itself. Done in about 25 minutes without even breaking a sweat.

"Old yeller?" for CODGER was a favorite, but is the question mark needed? Why? An old, grumpy (typically male) person might be called a CODGER. Is the point of the "?" something more than "Oh, look at the clever clue. We're punning on a the title of an old (and very good) book/film?"

Hmm, maybe CODGER hit closer to home than I realized ...

Loved the theme clues and answers. So very clever. Had to share them with my car-loving husband who actually laughed. He’s sharing the BUCKET SEATS with a friend who just bought a second-hand convertible.
Chewy and sexy like a Friday puzzle, but strutting its stuff like a Wednesday puzzle. I'll two scoops please!

Hilarious theme! I had a fun time imagining what that sloppy jalopy would have looked like. I think I just dated myself badly by using 'jalopy'.  I confess that I've been watching too many re-runs of old 1950s-60s sitcoms, now that I'm retired from the rat race.  Wait... is rat race still used?  Sigh.
A very fun Sunday. It was zippy, but so clever and silly. Nice way to start the day!
Wonderfully entertaining!

Quite a puzzle. Not all that easy for me, of course, but just had a good time working it all out. And, of course, a puzzle find today. A Sunday from December 3, 1978 by Alfio Micci with the title: "Reverse Versions." Some theme answers: BADFORNOTHING AFTERHAND GOODMINTON FRONTGAMMON BEFOREMATH UPTOEARTH UNDERNIGHTBAG OVERTHEWEATHER DOWNHOLSTERING Here's that link: https://www.xwordinfo.com/PS?date=12/3/1978&h=44d I'm done. ....
The clues started my morning with so many chuckles and laughs!  Thank you!

I’ve done the crossword daily for two years’ running and never felt compelled to comment until today. Thank you for a delightful puzzle that had me giggling throughout. I love puns in general but this running (or was it?) joke was exceptionally well executed and satisfying. Can’t wait for your next collaboration!

As others have said maybe just a tiny touch on the easy side but loads and loads of fun. Like many folks I'd wager, solving the Sunday puzzle with a lazy cup of coffee on a quiet morning is one of my favorite times of any week. I thoroughly enjoyed this one. Thanks, Ralph and Doug!
Starter car?? This is a finisher car!

As others have already said, but I must add, this a very fun puzzle that actually had me chuckling many times as I deduced the original theme fills.
A great way to spend a Sunday morning with a few cups of coffee.  Who hasn’t sold a used car that had some questionable underlying problems?  It brought me back to the sale of my first car to a somewhat naive buyer.  A Corvair (remember them?) that I had to divest myself of prior to entering the Army.  Caveat emptor!
Some may say the puzzle was too easy, but I found it to be in my Goldilocks zone. 
Nice job guys!

All is forgiven!  This puzzle makes up for some of the disappointing, exclusive, and Byzantine offerings that have saddened CrossWorld...  !

The guffaws just kept coming!  I start my solves at the bottom, and got QUIET RIDE early on, to my delight.  If PhysDau had been here, she might have gotten some just off the clues; I needed a few letters to suggest the next clever application of all the car-salesman-lingo...  DHubby is making breakfast (grits and eggs; I made shrimp and grits last night) and I kept reading clue/entry winners to entertain him.

This was just a TON of fun.....and I even plan to read the column and  of course the Constructors' notes.  
Loved it despite the many unknowns... (Harry Potter at the bottom of the ocean:  a good start...)

Well, I should stop and save some superlatives for later.

I’m glad I read the accompanying column today.  The humor was totally lost on me during the puzzle as I just plugged away on the adjacent clues, paying little attention to the absolutely hilarious theme!

I was very excited to get a rare Sunday gold, only to read the comments on the ease of the puzzle! [crying emoji here]. Oh well, the solve was hilarious throughout. Great fun and even better with some champs and the mandatory eye-dropper of OJ to make it a mimosa. Cheers folks.
Wonderfully misleading!    Ever consider adding a way for readers to rate puzzles?  I'd give this one a 10!

In keeping with the theme, your mileage may vary, but for me, this is just what I want from a Sunday puzzle.  Funny theme, mid-level difficulty, a few "it could be this word or it could be that word" answers...  this puzzle and a mug of black coffee made for a good morning.
Laughing out loud as I work through the puzzle. Love it!
Loved this one! Pretty easy and quick for a Sunday, but I was chuckling the whole way!
Quick drive but lots of laughs. Thanks Ralph and Doug!
Click and Clack would have loved this puzzle!!
Thanks for some real laughs this morning. Much fun.
Filled in the themes answers pretty quickly,...mainly because I think it describes a car I bought many years ago!  Fun Sunday puzzle.
Fun puzzle! No bells and whistles, just knowledge, creativity, and wit.
This was a fun puzzle! I loved solving all the theme clues and envisioning these two slimy car dealers trying to offload their jalopy. Like an old vaudeville act! What a joy!

I was the unfortunate owner of a used 73 Pinto for a while. On the day the stick shift came off in my hand while driving (just one of many problems) I remember thinking I could sell it and imply it was an automatic. “NO STICK!”

This puzzle reminded me of a Volvo we once had, which had a tricky and (in my view) unreliable manual choke. I often had trouble starting the car.

My husband loved that car, and as part of his defense, he would tout the safety record of Volvos. This was true, especially if half the time you couldn't get out of the driveway.

This was very entertaining. 

It was easy, yes, but outlasted my first cup of coffee and I still had some blanks to mull over after two passes through the clues. I'll take it.

I seemed to want sandED instead of IRONED. I do neither these days, but have nice memories of the former. Woodworking really is a satisfying art.
LOVED this puzzle! Exceptional cluing, IMO, and chuckled aloud several times. My favorite answer was to the “struck by lightning” clue. Well done, Ralph! Keep ‘em coming.

My only semi-muscle car I ever had was a 1968 Mercury Cougar.  It was so sleek and beautiful, but in the few months I had it I had to have a new automatic transmission put in, and it wouldn't start when the car was warm.

None of the mechanics in town could fix it.

I told a guy I worked with that I was going to sell it for parts.

He said, "No, you can't do that."  

I said, "Why not?"

He said, "Because none of the parts work."

He was sadly right.

And a dollar short.
I just solved yesterday's puzzle and I must interrupt today's proceedings to say I just love Saturday's 17A clue and answer.  I don't get to type DIADELOSMUERTOS often enough.
Thank you for indulging me.  This was not a cry for attention.
Looking forward to more puzzles from Ralph Sharaga and Doug Peterson.

Too much fun!! Congratulations, Ralph (with Doug!) on such a spectacular debut!! Never have vehicle lemons sounded so good -- I was laughing out loud throughout my solve!🚙🍋😂

Hope to see more from you very soon! Thanks for the most entertaining Sunday Drive I've had in years!😄

Normally I am not a pun fan, they generally go over my head. But this was so much fun! I’ve had enough old bangers in my time that each clue raised a memory and a chuckle. I used to get ancient Renaults through a friend who specialised n breaking them. He’d find me a model that could be fixed up enough to get through one MOT (UK vehicle fitness test), that would give me one year’s driving before it was scrapped. I drove some magnificent old coaches, with bench seats as deep as a sofa and a steering wheel the size of a cartwheel. A full tank of fuel would double the car’s value. Happy days.

Oh, the puzzle. Great. Yes a Tad easier for a Sunday, but still chewy enough in places to make me ponder, especially the obligatory unknown celebrities. Was v pleased with myself that I got REVERE from just -E-R-. Had Irani for OMANI which held up that corner, but got there in the end.

More please.
This was really excellent!! Looking forward to seeing more from them.

Solved quickly, and really enjoyable. Lots of very fresh and clever cluing of common fill, little if any pop trivia, and an amusing theme that entertained as it developed from top to bottom.
Great fun!
really enjoyable sunday, my partner and i were cackling throughout. great debut! <3
Not only did they construct both NY and LA Times puzzles, they used the same clue/answer in both.

Cargo space? 

No, car go road, car no fly.

It seems I had a bumpier ride than most, mainly because I confidently filled in several answers that fit but were still quite wrong. “Head boy” instead of PREFECT, for example, and “repeated” instead of TOLL FREE.  But as I figured out my mistakes, the road opened up and suddenly it felt like the autobahn.

What a clever theme, with genuinely funny entries. This is what I call a great Sunday drive.
A very fun solve today! Love me some good puns!

@NYC Traveler
I just saw your question from yesterday and replied.
This was the most fun I’ve had with crosswords in a long time! Thank You Ralph and Doug!
seriously, never had so much fun. Make more.
What a delightful and perfectly enjoyable Sunday puzzle! Thumbs up!
Totally thought 94D was “sativa” at first…
SOOOOO fun! Word learned today: FEN. Thanks for the fun and well-constructed puzzle. I laughed out loud multiple times on the theme clues. Lovely Sunday.
Probably my favorite theme puzzle since the Minesweeper one. The bad-car-ad puns were so hilarious my partner wanted me to screenshot them so they could have them and laugh. A+

Furrowed brow over what appears to be an odd coincidence. For no reason I can explain, I decided to do a search for: 
BILLIONAIRE

And... it appeared in 3 puzzles: 

A Friday in 2003
A Friday in 2004
A Friday in 2005 

Hmmm.... 

...
Loved this puzzle because it made me laugh out loud!
Ralph and Doug, I gotta tell ya, this puzzle was a real treat from start to finish. All the themers and their clues were funny and priceless. I had a lotta fun with this one – thanks!
This was very funny and fun to puzzle out.

I miss the second Sunday puzzle blogs: so I am writing here to praise today's PandA by Evan Kalish. How refreshing and fun!  Many original clues today and thoroughly enjoyable PUNS which made me laugh out loud.  A great 'punny' Sunday double header!
Couldn’t figure out how SARI is a homophone for SORRY, then remembered that I’m in 🇨🇦… 🤣

Love reading all the reminiscences about car experiences.  I have a checkered past! First car - a '71 Buick LeSabre in 1981 with rust holes galore $300. Followed by an '81 bright yellow Chevette - yes, I had a 'vette! Then a brand new Renault Alliance - "Car of the year 1983"! I've also owned 2 Neons and a Saturn Ion. 
Favorite Cars: 1987 Nissan Stanza Wagon - Google it. Super cool. Felt like the Chariot in Lost in Space. AND my son's first car, a '96 Thunderbird. Blew a head gasket. What I wouldn't give to have that car back.

Cleaned out the pop-up camper this week to get it ready to sell - and what should i turn up, but my copy of Merl Reagle's 100th Anniversary Crossword Book! My go-to relaxing in a patio chair, feet on a hassock, I'm under no time restraints but I'm using a pen pastime, ever. No rush, no fuss, just Merl cracking wise in Sunday size. This puzzle reminded me of his style, and I salute you. Also Merl, a genius gone way too soon. Cheers.
I loved this! Witty, funny and just an enjoyable solve!!
This one made me giggle! Good job!
I am totally in awe of the skill of each and every one of the crossword creators but this one is one of my favourite ever. Hats off to you gentlemen 🏆
Just curious:  Doesn't the word "malicious" always imply deliberate?

Clever, very clever! 

I'll ride with the writers any time
Tons of fun. Hated yesterday's, love today's.

I always enjoy the photo that accompanies Wordplay. Sometimes they appear to be random and other times, more obvious. But it's fun figuring out how they tie into the puzzle theme. A shout out to whoever is choosing these! (And a fun puzzle today too.)

Loved the theme.
I'm picturing the dad from the movie Breaking Away...
"Refund?!! Refund???!!!"
For me, best puzzle of the year using Misdirection . Fun, more if puzzable!
Shades of Car Talk! Congratulations, Ralph, and here’s hoping you’re back at the wheel again soon!
Two issues: 1) Pronounced correctly, "sari" and "sorry" aren't really homophones; 2) when referring to a level of a building, it's spelled "storey", not "story".
Giggling throughout. Fun.
Can't believe I didn't listen to yesterday's Car Talk podcast until just now. These are all replays, obviously. Yesterday they replayed their call from Will Shortz.

I really like the theme today with the seedy used car salesman jokes.  Sold ASIS.

Northeast corner was tough for me.  I don’t see how any non Harry Potter fans could possibly know an advanced trivia detail from it.  And the meaning of the STREAKS clue didn’t hit me till after I got it with crossings.

Thank you Mr. Sharaga and Mr. Peterson for that beautiful, fun puzzle.  I have not laughed and smiled so much before while doing a crossword puzzle, and I hate to admit I've been doing them for too many decades.  Congratulations on a fine debut.  And I hope to see more of your collaborations down the road.
I had WELLMET instead of GALLANT, some good misdirection all around with this puzzle
Great puzzle for Gen Xers!
What a wonderful, engaging humorous puzzle!
That was a hoot from start to finish - thank you for the fun!
I giggled along with everyone, and also set a personal best time for a Sunday puzzle. I couldn't be more pleased.

I loved this Sunday!  I laughed along with all the themers once I got the trick (I tend to skip through the long ones first go-around and have the crosses help me out).  It was such a cute theme and was fun from start to finish!
10 down brought me back to my childhood of reading Highlights magazine (fun with a Purpose) and keeping up to date with the antics of Goofus and GALLANT

Fun and funny! Please do some more.

One clue that tripped me up was "Made smooth."
 _ _ ONED. I kept wanting to put ST in the first two spaces. 

Cheers
Loved this puzzle. It was like sharing my Sunday with Merl Reagle once again. What fun! I'm 89 and I needed this. More, please.

"A better travel alternative"
RAIL

@Barry Ancona
Rafa again subbing for Rex Parker called it Medium-Challenging, after giving yesterday's a rating of Medium-Hard. Interesting that he can construct a good puzzle, but fund of knowledge seems to be lacking. Most solvers here found this to be Wednesday-ish.

@Barry Ancona

That's what makes it the burlap sack of sites. I wouldn't make much of it.

I find the 'constructor vanity' canard puzzling.
Don't we want constructors to be clever? Can one really be 'too clever', or does that just mean 'cleverer than me'?

@Charles Peterson

I canardly disagree that that is a possibility.

@SP

I’m not Indian, so there’s a chance I’ve been pronouncing “sari” wrong. But I think the real issue may be the pronunciation of “sorry”, and that is mostly regional. Some (especially those in states near Canada) say “sore-y”, while others (me) pronounce it more like “sah-ry”, which to my ears is the same as “sari”.
@SP I am Indian and this clue definitely threw me off. It is pronounced “saah-ree”, not sorry. It is also the first time I realized this mispronunciation exists.

@Yashaswi

But how do you pronounce sorry?

@Grumpy
